We have long warned everyone not to disclose sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, since most companies use such content as training data—but now there is an even more serious reason to be doubly vigilant.

The situation deteriorated rapidly over the weekend, when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat records could be obtained through a simple Google search……

Leakage of Claude chat conversations

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family members. The chatbot generates a link for you to send to one or more designated recipients, and Claude also assures users that even people who know the URL cannot view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users found that viewing these conversations actually does not require a link at all. Whether by entering specific search terms or simply instructing Google to display all chat records shared in this manner, one can easily find them via Google search. BBC News reported as follows:

In practice, you only need to tell Google Search the directory Claude uses for sharing conversations (i.e., site:claude.ai/share), and everything is laid out in plain view.

As you might expect, some of the conversation contents are utterly bizarre—for instance, someone asking why the recording industry is covering up the fact that birds co-produced most of Jay-Z's albums. But other conversations contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private dialogues; a lawyer inquiring whether he needed to proactively disclose a violation; and a user who, while asking for help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet, inadvertently leaked his private key.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this is not a problem.

In reality, this is clearly a serious problem, because it is entirely not what users would have expected to happen. To make matters worse, Wired's report points out that the root cause appears to involve extreme negligence.

Prior to this, yesterday's news already reported that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox environment on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to protect yourself

The issue seems to have been at least partially addressed—previously visible search results can no longer be loaded—but given that this feature relies on the principle of "security through obscurity," I recommend that everyone avoid using the sharing function.

I also recommend deleting all previously shared chat records. You can go to "Settings" > "Privacy" > "Shared Conversations" > "Manage" to delete them.

Once again proves the superiority of Apple's approach

Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri adopt a three-tier architecture to safeguard privacy:

  • Where feasible, AI processing is completed on-device
  • The first fallback option is Apple's own server called Private Cloud Compute (PCC)
  • Only as a last resort will the Gemini model, which carries PCC-equivalent safeguards, be used

The highly sophisticated PCC architecture ensures that neither Apple nor Google can access any data, nor will it be retained. The security architecture designed by Apple allows independent security researchers to verify this claim.
